assessment.title: Year 5 Fractions and Percentages Combined Assessment

authorised_variations.statement: Questions 7 and 8 may use related denominators.

curriculum.description: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator using flexible and efficient strategies
Identify the use of percentages in everyday situations and recognise that 100% represents a complete whole, which is equal to one
Determine a familiar fraction, decimal or percentage of a whole number

authorisation.statement: For Question 6, make it about finding 10% of a quantity.

questions.prompt: Use the fraction strips to calculate {{frac:3:8:q1-a}} + {{frac:2:8:q1-b}}.
solution_steps: Combine three eighths and two eighths to obtain five eighths.
questions.student_task_restatement: Combine the two same-denominator fractions shown by the strips and record the total.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks whether the student combines equal-sized parts while preserving the denominator.

mark_evidence.evidence: Records five eighths as the sum.

representation.kind: aligned fraction strips divided into eighths
representation.mathematical_purpose: Makes the equal-sized parts and the additive combination visible.

visual_spec.purpose: Make equal-sized eighths available as mathematical evidence for the addition.
information_carried: The shaded parts may be combined
visual_spec.removal_effect: The question would no longer assess calculation from the stated visual model.
visual_spec.student_action: Read and combine the represented eighths.
accessibility_cues: Equal partitions remain distinguishable in greyscale
Labels and boundaries do not rely on colour alone

response_space.mathematical_justification: Separates the final symbolic total from the two source strips.

prompt_audit_tokens: Use the fraction strips to calculate

questions.prompt: A bottle is 100% full. Write the number of complete wholes represented by 100%.
solution_steps: Recognise that 100% represents one complete whole.
questions.student_task_restatement: Connect 100% with the number of complete wholes it represents.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks the foundational equivalence between 100% and one complete whole.
observable_evidence: Correct equivalence of 100% and one whole

mark_evidence.evidence: Records that 100% represents one complete whole.

representation.omission_reason: The item checks the direct 100%-to-one-whole equivalence before later visual and contextual applications.

response_space.mathematical_justification: The equality is the mathematical relationship the student must complete.

questions.prompt: One whole is shown. Use the strip to model 1 − {{frac:3:8:q3-subtrahend}}, then calculate.
solution_steps: Partition the whole into eight equal parts and mark three parts as removed.
Count the five remaining eighths.
questions.student_task_restatement: Show three eighths removed from one whole and record the amount left.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks whether the student treats one whole as eight eighths before subtracting.
observable_evidence: Correct removal shown on the strip

mark_evidence.evidence: Shows three of the eight equal parts removed from the whole strip.
Records the remainder as five eighths.

representation.kind: editable whole strip partitioned into eighths
representation.mathematical_purpose: Elicits conversion of one whole to eight eighths and shows the removed parts.

visual_spec.purpose: Provide an exact partitioned whole on which the student can model subtraction.
information_carried: One whole contains eight equal parts
visual_spec.removal_effect: The required modelling action and its observable evidence would be removed.
visual_spec.student_action: Mark three eighths as removed and interpret the remainder.
accessibility_cues: Partition boundaries remain visible in greyscale
Student marks need not rely on colour

questions.prompt: For each situation, decide whether the percentage is less than one whole or more than one whole: a battery backup at 65% and a poster target at 120%.
questions.answer: 65% is less than one whole; 120% is more than one whole.
solution_steps: Compare 65% with 100% and classify it as less than one whole.
Compare 120% with 100% and classify it as more than one whole.
questions.student_task_restatement: Classify each percentage by comparing it with the complete whole, 100%.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks whether the student uses 100% as the reference whole for values below and above one whole.

mark_evidence.evidence: Classifies 65% as less than one whole.
Classifies 120% as more than one whole.

representation.omission_reason: The item assesses direct comparison with the 100% reference and a visual would supply an unnecessary cue.

response_space.mathematical_justification: The two response labels are the mathematical categories students must apply to separate contexts.

questions.prompt: Combine the strips to calculate {{frac:7:10:q5-a}} + {{frac:6:10:q5-b}}. Show a valid strategy and use a different calculation or representation to check your result.
solution_steps: Combine seven tenths and six tenths to obtain thirteen tenths.
Record the sum as thirteen tenths.
Check using a different method, such as showing one whole and three tenths on the strips.
questions.student_task_restatement: Combine the tenths, record the fraction total and verify it in a different way.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks whether the student can add beyond one whole while preserving the denominator and verify the result independently.

mark_evidence.evidence: Shows a valid strategy that combines seven tenths and six tenths.
Records the total as thirteen tenths.
Uses a different valid calculation or representation to verify thirteen tenths.

representation.kind: two editable fraction strips divided into tenths
representation.mathematical_purpose: Shows the combined thirteen tenths extending beyond one whole without changing the size of each part.

visual_spec.purpose: Represent equal tenths across two strips while preserving the need to select a combining strategy.
information_carried: The combined amount may exceed one whole
visual_spec.removal_effect: The item would cease to assess addition and verification using fraction strips.
visual_spec.student_action: Combine the represented tenths and use the diagram as one possible check.
accessibility_cues: Equal partitions remain distinguishable in greyscale
Boundaries and labels do not rely on colour alone

prompt_audit_tokens: use a different calculation or representation to check

questions.prompt: The school library has 240 new books. Ten per cent will be placed in a display. How many books will be displayed? Show your method and use a different calculation or representation to check your answer.
solution_steps: Connect 10% with one tenth or dividing by ten.
Calculate 240 divided by ten to obtain 24 books.
Verify with a different representation or calculation, such as ten equal groups of 24.
questions.student_task_restatement: Find ten per cent of 240 books and verify the result using a genuinely different method or representation.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks the explicitly authorised Year 6 connection between 10% and division by ten, including independent verification.

mark_evidence.evidence: Shows that 10% is found by dividing the whole quantity by ten or by an equivalent method.
Calculates and records 24 books.
Uses a different valid calculation or representation to verify 24.

representation.omission_reason: Students choose their own second representation or calculation; supplying one would prompt the verification strategy.

prompt_audit_tokens: Ten per cent will be placed in a display

questions.prompt: A ribbon roll was 2 m long. Maya cut {{frac:5:8:q7-a}} m for a sash and {{frac:3:4:q7-b}} m for a border. After she cut one more piece, {{frac:1:4:q7-c}} m of ribbon was left. How long was the third piece? Show how you worked it out and check that all the ribbon lengths total 2 m.
solution_steps: Rename three quarters as six eighths and one quarter as two eighths.
Add the known cut and remaining lengths to obtain thirteen eighths.
Rename 2 m as sixteen eighths and subtract to obtain three eighths for the third piece.
Check that five eighths, six eighths, three eighths and two eighths total sixteen eighths or 2 m.
questions.student_task_restatement: Work backwards from the whole roll, two known cuts and the remainder to find the missing cut, then verify the complete total.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks transfer of same-denominator fraction operations to a reverse, related-denominator context with a whole-total check.

mark_evidence.evidence: Renames the quarter quantities as eighths or otherwise establishes a valid common representation.
Correctly combines the known cut and remaining lengths as thirteen eighths.
Finds the third piece as three eighths of a metre.
Checks all cut lengths and the remainder total 2 m.

representation.omission_reason: Extracting the related lengths and relationships from prose is part of the assessed reasoning.

prompt_audit_tokens: A ribbon roll was 2 m long
How long was the third piece

extracted_information: first cut is five eighths of a metre
second cut is three quarters of a metre
remainder is one quarter of a metre

questions.prompt: A class completed 65% of its original reading goal. During the next week, it recorded another 55% of the original goal, but 15% of the original goal had been counted in both records. The teacher had also increased the complete goal to 125% of the original goal. The display then read, ‘New goal: 100% complete.’ Is the display correct? Determine the corrected total as a percentage of the original goal and explain whether the original and new goals were complete.
questions.answer: The corrected total is 105% of the original goal. The original goal is complete, but the 125% new goal is not complete, so the display is incorrect.
solution_steps: Combine the two records, then remove the duplicated 15 percentage points: 65% + 55% − 15% = 105%.
Compare 105% with the original complete whole, 100%, to decide the original goal is complete.
Compare 105% with the revised complete goal, 125%, to decide the new goal is incomplete.
Conclude that the display is incorrect because the reference whole for the new goal is 125% of the original goal.
questions.student_task_restatement: Correct the overlapping records and compare the result with both reference wholes before judging the display.
questions.diagnostic_purpose: Checks sustained reference-whole reasoning when data overlap and the complete target changes.

mark_evidence.evidence: Subtracts the duplicated 15 percentage points once from the combined records.
Determines the corrected total as 105% of the original goal.
Explains that 105% means the original 100% goal is complete.
Explains that 105% is below the revised 125% goal and therefore the display is incorrect.

representation.omission_reason: The student must extract and coordinate the overlapping records and two reference wholes from sentences.

prompt_audit_tokens: completed 65% of its original reading goal

extracted_information: first record is 65% of the original goal
second record is 55% of the original goal
the revised whole is 125% of the original goal
